<a name="multi-part-download"></a>
## Multi-Part Download (MPD)

Multi-part download (MPD), also referred to as *parallel download*, sees substantial improvements in 4.3 across the Python SDK, Go client APIs, and [`aisloader`](/docs/aisloader.md).

> For a detailed walkthrough of the architecture, benchmarks, and PyTorch integration,
> see the companion blog post: [Parallel Download: 9x Lower Latency for Large-Object Reads](https://aistore.nvidia.com/blog/2026/03/25/parallel-download).

On the [Python side](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/tree/main/python/aistore/sdk/obj/content_iterator), the parallel downloader has been reworked to use multiprocessing together with shared-memory buffers. This replaces the earlier thread-based design with a model that better matches the underlying I/O pattern: worker processes perform range reads in parallel and write directly into shared memory.

> This currently requires the `fork` start method and is therefore Linux-only.

Two parallel download modes are now supported:

**Streaming (`create_iter`)** keeps a fixed number of range reads in flight and yields data incrementally via a shared-memory ring buffer.

**Bulk (`read_all`)** uses a full-object shared-memory buffer (`ParallelBuffer`). Workers write directly into their assigned byte ranges - thus reducing the copy count and associated (CPU, memory) overhead.
The caller receives the completed buffer without the extra copy previously required on the return path. The caller is responsible for releasing the buffer via `close()` or by using the context manager protocol.

This is especially relevant for large-object workloads, where removing the extra assembly step reduces overhead and makes parallel full-object reads more efficient.

For PyTorch users, 4.3 also adds [`AISParallelMapDataset`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/tree/main/python/aistore/pytorch), a new map-style dataset for parallel large-object downloads. It wraps `read_all()` with `num_workers` and returns `(object_name, ParallelBuffer)` from `__getitem__`, leaving buffer consumption and cleanup to the collate function or training loop.

> `AISParallelMapDataset` is currently **experimental.** Further optimization - including memory footprint - is planned in subsequent releases.

On the Go side, [`MultipartDownloadStream`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/blob/main/api/mpt.go) now returns object attributes together with the stream reader. This makes it easier for callers to validate checksums and reuse metadata discovered during the initial HEAD request.

Benchmarking support has expanded as well. [`aisloader`](/docs/aisloader.md) now supports `--mpdstream` as a GET workload variant, with configurable chunk size and worker count, optional checksum verification, and separate statistics for multipart-download operations.

Highlights include:

- multiprocessing-based parallel download in the [Python SDK](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/tree/main/python/aistore/sdk)
- shared-memory bulk reads via `ParallelBuffer`, avoiding the extra copy previously needed by parallel `read_all()`
- new [`AISParallelMapDataset`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/tree/main/python/aistore/pytorch) for PyTorch-based large-object training and data-loading workflows
- Go [`MultipartDownloadStream`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/blob/main/api/mpt.go) returning object attributes together with the stream
- new [`aisloader`](/docs/aisloader.md) MPD workload mode and reporting

### Commits

* [285e885d9](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/285e885d9): `sdk/python`: parallel object download via full-size buffer with `read_all()`
* [a8faf7a11](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/a8faf7a11): `sdk/python`: update parallel downloader to use multiprocessing
* [a0315e845](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/a0315e845): `aisloader`: add multipart download stream operation for benchmark

<a name="multi-part-upload-whole-object-checksum"></a>
## Multi-Part Upload: Whole-Object Checksum

During multipart upload, parts may arrive out of order. Because computing a whole-object checksum previously required re-reading the assembled payload, AIS did not compute whole-object checksums for cloud buckets. In 4.3, AIS computes whole-object CRC32C without rereading data: each part is checksummed as it arrives, and once all parts are present AIS combines the per-part CRC32C values algebraically, regardless of upload order.

Whole-object checksum is now enabled unconditionally. When all parts are present, the whole-object CRC32C is derived from the per-part values using [cos.CRC32CCombine](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/blob/main/cmn/cos/cksum.go) - a GF(2) matrix exponentiation over the Castagnoli polynomial that runs in O(log N) in the length of each part, with no I/O. Parts may arrive in any order.

Additionally, when parts do arrive in order, AIS also computes bucket-configured streaming checksum and stores it as part of object metadata.

### Commits

* [f80d245e6](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/f80d245e6): `chunks`: add `CRC32C` checksum combination support; major refactoring
* [d2b85401d](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/d2b85401d): `chunks`: enable `CRC32C` checksum computation for cloud buckets

## Global Rebalance

[Global rebalance](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/blob/main/docs/rebalance.md) continues to improve in 4.3, especially under load and in the presence of lazy-delete backlog.

Improvements include:

- scale-out of rebalance workers
- improved lazy-delete responsiveness and logging
- on-the-wire ACK tracking refinements using terminal values
- improved handling when there are no active targets before or after rebalance start
- larger burst-buffer allowance to tolerate lazy-delete backlog

The result is a more predictable rebalance path, with better visibility and fewer cases where lazy-delete pressure interferes with forward progress.

<a name="authentication-and-key-management"></a>
## Authentication and Key Management

Authentication and authorization capabilities underwent substantial operational hardening.

The release adds persistent JWKS state, manual key rotation, and public-key retrieval, while also improving configuration validation, token-signing abstractions, retry behavior, and operational diagnostics.

It also completes the transition toward standard JWT claim semantics. The previously deprecated custom username and expires claims are now removed. Issued AuthN tokens now additionally carry standard `iss`, `iat`, and `aud` claims.

From an operational perspective, the main changes include:

- previously deprecated custom `username` and `expires` JWT claims removed (see [Upgrade Notes](#upgrade-notes))
- issued AuthN JWTs now include standard `iss`, `iat`, and `aud` claims
- JWKS persistence to the AuthN database
- public-key retrieval API
- manual key-rotation API with JWKS accumulation (old keys retained for token validation)
- new `KeyProvider` / `ServerKeyProvider` interfaces replacing the prior ad-hoc signing dispatch
- improved validation and defaults for AuthN configuration
- clearer error messages for invalid configuration
- passphrase-based encryption of RSA private keys
- retry support for selected transient AuthN failures

Together, these changes make AuthN easier to operate, safer to configure, and better suited for long-running production deployments. Run `ais auth login` after upgrade; see [Upgrade Notes](#upgrade-notes).

<a name="media-aware-worker-parallelism"></a>
## Media-Aware Worker Parallelism

AIS now detects backing media characteristics at startup and uses a shared runtime policy to auto-scale default worker counts by [mountpath](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/blob/main/docs/terminology.md#mountpath) count and storage type (HDD, SSD, NVMe), while still throttling under high goroutine, memory, or CPU pressure.

The result is better out-of-the-box parallelism for jobs such as:

- all multi-object operations (prefetch, multi-object copy/transform, evict, and more)
- transform/copy bucket
- blob-download
- global rebalance

### Commits

* [8de9d4f44](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/8de9d4f44): Mountpath media detection: HDD, SSD, and NVMe
* [259fa2885](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/259fa2885): Media-aware worker scaling for xactions, TCB, and blob-download
* [9a22f67b0](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/9a22f67b0): Slow-filesystem handling and mountpath media reporting

<a name="object-head-v2"></a>
## Object HEAD v2

The new API to provide object properties was first included in v4.2.

Introduced as experimental, the API is now stable in 4.3 and is used broadly across CLI and backend flows.

> The original (v1) API serialized all object metadata unconditionally - erasure-coding, n-way mirror, and location fields were always included in every response regardless of whether the caller needed them. With the new API, the fields are only populated and transmitted when explicitly requested, resulting in smaller responses and lower marshaling overhead (for the common case) when callers need only a subset of all supported attributes.

Changes in this area include:

- `ais show object` migration to `HeadObjectV2`
- remote AIS `HeadObj` migration to `HeadObjectV2`
- default property sets for object HEAD v2
- continued cleanup around metadata behavior for cached and remote objects

These changes reduce metadata overhead and align more client and backend paths with the newer API.

### Commits

* [5911c62a0](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/5911c62a0): Define default property sets for Object HEAD v2
* [5e99f722e](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/5e99f722e): Migrate `ais show object` to `HeadObjectV2`
* [7241c932a](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/7241c932a): Migrate remote AIS `HeadObj` to `HeadObjectV2`

<a name="rechunk-remote-bucket-sync"></a>
## Rechunk: Remote Bucket Support and `--sync-remote`

Introduced in 4.1, `rechunk` xaction is a batch job that rewrites existing objects between monolithic and chunked layouts according to current bucket settings - for example:

```console
$ ais bucket props s3://abc chunks
PROPERTY                         VALUE
chunks.checkpoint_every          0
chunks.chunk_size                1GiB
chunks.flags                     0
chunks.max_monolithic_size       1TiB
chunks.objsize_limit             0B (auto-chunking disabled)
```

Previously, `rechunk` operated exclusively on in-cluster objects and always skipped the remote backend. This release extends `rechunk` to support remote buckets, with an explicit [`SyncRemote`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/blob/main/api/apc/rechunk.go) option controlling whether rechunked objects are written back to remote storage via multipart upload.

The default for remote buckets remains local-only - `rechunk` rewrites the local representation without touching the backend. With `SyncRemote=true` (or `--sync-remote` in the CLI), AIS uploads the rewritten objects back to S3, GCS, Azure, OCI, or remote AIS - making the new layout persistent in remote storage as well.

See also:
* [Rechunk control message](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/blob/main/api/apc/rechunk.go)
* [Go `api.RechunkBucket`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/blob/main/api/bucket.go)

### Commits

* [18c04f98b](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/18c04f98b): `rechunk`: extend support for remote buckets; add `sync-remote` option
* [f1d6328fe](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/f1d6328fe): `cli/rechunk`: update API usage; add `--sync-remote` flag

<a name="runtime-backend-and-reliability-fixes"></a>
## Runtime, Backend, and Reliability Fixes

Beyond the larger feature work, 4.3 includes a number of robustness and interoperability improvements across runtime paths and backend integrations.

Notable fixes and updates include:

- improved Go client retry behavior with correct request-body reopening
- intra-cluster TLS x509 certificate reload fix: dedicated self-contained `_x509Client()`/`_x509call()` helpers using `InsecureSkipVerify` and `Transport.Clone()`, replacing the prior approach that used a stale TLS client during broadcast
- AWS chunked-content upload support (`sigv4-streaming`)
- cgroup-aware CPU starvation detection, replacing load-average-based heuristics
- ETL initialization race fix: IC registration deferred until after 2PC begin
- clearer remote AIS backend error reporting with cluster identity prefix

Collectively, these fixes reduce operational "surprises" and improve reliability in long-running deployments.

* [632387267](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/632387267): Dedicated insecure client for x509 reload control path
* [909b69513](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/909b69513): Support AWS chunked content encoding (`sigv4-streaming`)

<a name="build-ci-and-tools"></a>
## Build, CI, and Tools

Build and CI changes in this release include multi-architecture Docker build updates for selected images, a redesigned minimal Docker deployment (see below), [aisloader](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/blob/main/docs/aisloader.md) support for benchmarking multi-part downloads, and assorted dependency and workflow updates.

Related Kubernetes deployment and operator changes are covered briefly in the next section.

All user-facing AIS container images are now also available with native support for `arm64` hosts. This reduces emulation overhead and should improve performance on ARM-based machines.

### Kubernetes deployment

The Kubernetes-side AIStore tooling also advanced alongside 4.3. In the separate [`ais-k8s`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/ais-k8s) repository, the AIS Operator and Helm charts were updated for 4.3 compatibility, with improvements spanning auth credential injection, configurable probe timings, PVC retention behavior, rollout and reconciliation logic, `arm64` image support, and deployment tooling such as cloud-init and sysctl tuning scripts.

The deployment guide was also simplified, and older playbook-based deployment guidance was deprecated in favor of the operator-centered path.

Assorted commits in this **separate** repo include:

* [935b2ba](https://github.com/NVIDIA/ais-k8s/commit/935b2ba): `helm/authn`: rewrite chart for 4.3 compatibility
* [e8ea56c](https://github.com/NVIDIA/ais-k8s/commit/e8ea56c): operator: support auth creds injection for admin client
* [8894228](https://github.com/NVIDIA/ais-k8s/commit/8894228): operator: allow probe timings to be configured
* [c53ef57](https://github.com/NVIDIA/ais-k8s/commit/c53ef57): operator: allow configuring PVC retention policy
* [c1339e2](https://github.com/NVIDIA/ais-k8s/commit/c1339e2): operator: add native support for arm64 hosts with multi-arch image build targets
* [ea91e4a](https://github.com/NVIDIA/ais-k8s/commit/ea91e4a): docs: deprecate playbook deployment; simplify deployment guide

### Minimal Docker Deployment

The minimal Docker deployment - a quick way to spin up a fully functional single-node AIS cluster (one proxy/gateway, one target) without Kubernetes or a full bare-metal setup - has been redesigned as a proper two-container Docker Compose setup.

The previous implementation ran both proxy and target as backgrounded processes inside a single container, which made independent lifecycle management impossible.

The new [setup](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/tree/main/deploy/prod/docker/compose) gives each role its own container, a shared internal network, healthcheck-gated startup (target waits for proxy to be healthy before joining), and named volumes for persistent storage.

Changes:

- **Podman and Docker support** - auto-detected; override with `COMPOSE="docker compose"`
- **Cloud backends** - AWS credentials via env vars or `~/.aws` directory mount (`AWS_CREDENTIALS_PATH`); GCP via service account JSON mount (`GCP_CREDENTIALS_PATH`); image built with `aws gcp azure` support
- **Makefile targets** - `make up`, `make up-build`, `make down`, `make clean`, `make logs`, `make status`
- **Pre-built image** - `aistorage/cluster-minimal:latest` on DockerHub; `make up` pulls automatically

See [deploy/prod/docker/compose/README.md](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/blob/main/deploy/prod/docker/compose/README.md) for quick start and full reference.

### aisloader: Multipart Download Stream Benchmark

`aisloader` now supports benchmarking [multi-part download](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/blob/main/docs/aisloader.md#multipart-download-stream) via new command line:

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--pctmpdstream` | `0` | Percentage of GET operations using MPD stream |
| `--mpdstream-chunk-size` | `8 MiB` | Chunk size for parallel download |
| `--mpdstream-workers` | `16` | Number of concurrent download workers (`0` = API default) |

MPD stream operations appear as `GET-MPDSTREAM` in interval stats output and are tracked separately from regular GETs and get-batch. Checksum verification is supported via `--verify-hash`.

> Note: `--pctmpdstream` is mutually exclusive with `--pctput` and `--batch-size`.

### Commits

* [a88f4bd41](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/a88f4bd41): Multi-arch Docker builds for ais-util, authn, and cluster-minimal
* [e865c5043](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/e865c5043): Stabilize CI jobs and corner cases; rebalance timeout to 3m
* [3343decdb](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/3343decdb): Bump OpenTelemetry; refresh modules

<a name="upgrade-notes"></a>
## Upgrade Notes

### AuthN: token reissuance and JWT claim changes (clusters with authentication only)

> This section **only applies** to deployments that use [AuthN](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/blob/main/docs/authn.md).

Tokens issued by older AuthN versions are invalid after upgrade to 4.3. Run `ais auth login` after upgrading to obtain a new token (or see `ais auth login --help` for details).

The `aud` claim contains the cluster IDs the token is authorized for. AIS gateways can optionally enforce audience matching via `RequiredClaims.Aud` configuration. Admin tokens receive an `aud` claim set to all registered cluster IDs at the time of issuance. If new clusters are registered after an admin token is issued, the admin must re-authenticate to receive an updated audience.

### Bucket metadata (BMD) changes

Bucket metadata is extended with `extra.gcp` to support per-bucket GCP credentials. At the same time, obsolete legacy `extra.hdfs` fields are removed from the current metadata model. For compatibility, AIStore 4.3 continues to read older persisted metadata that still contains those legacy fields.

### Legacy S3 bucket inventory deprecated

The legacy S3-specific bucket-inventory path is now **deprecated** in favor of [native bucket inventory (NBI)](#native-bucket-inventory-nbi). This includes the older S3 inventory listing flow and related internal compatibility paths. Removal is planned for the next (**4.4**) release. Users relying on S3 inventory should migrate to NBI-based listing and inventory management.

> [`xmeta`: AIS Metadata Tool](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/blob/main/cmd/xmeta/README.md)

> As always, backing up cluster metadata (periodically and/or before upgrade) is recommended. In particular, archive metadata from the node configuration directory and, for storage targets, from all mountpaths. Keep the backup off-node.

# AIStore 4.4 Release Notes

Source: https://github.com/nvidia/aistore/blob/main/docs/relnotes/4.4.md

# AIStore 4.4 Release Notes

AIStore **4.4** is a short release cycle focused on runtime correctness, container awareness, and consolidation.

This release is the first to deliver full cgroup v2 support, improving AIS behavior in constrained and containerized deployments. CPU and memory accounting are now cgroup-aware, container detection and startup initialization are more robust, and CPU utilization is reported as a smoothed moving average rather than an instantaneous sample.

4.4 also promotes native bucket inventory (NBI) into the default AIS path for S3-compatible inventory workflows. The release adds non-recursive inventory listing, removes the legacy S3-specific inventory implementation, and updates the S3 compatibility layer to route inventory-backed requests through NBI. NBI should now be regarded as stable.

Additional changes improve S3 bucket region discovery and error reporting, add per-bucket OCI regions and instance principal authentication, introduce per-bucket user-defined custom metadata, and update the CLI, documentation, tracing, and build tooling.

This release includes roughly 50 commits since [4.3](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/releases/tag/v1.4.3) and is backward compatible except where noted below.

<a name="runtime-cgroup-v2-cpu-and-memory"></a>
## Runtime: cgroup v2, CPU, and Memory

The main feature of 4.4 is full **cgroup v2** support, with a broader runtime refactor to make AIS behave correctly in standard containers and restricted Kubernetes-style environments.

### See Also

* [AIS in Containerized Environments](/docs/containerized.md)

The work starts with startup and environment detection. AIS now initializes CPU and memory accounting earlier and more explicitly via `sys.Init()`, revises container auto-detection with additional heuristics, and adds the `ForceContainerCPUMem` feature flag to override failed detection when needed. The initialization path also applies container-aware CPU counting and `GOMAXPROCS`, and avoids repeatedly retrying failed cgroup parsing later at runtime.

On the memory side, AIS now supports **cgroup-v2 memory reporting** based on `memory.max`, `memory.current`, and `memory.stat`, while keeping `memory.stat` best-effort so that missing or unreadable auxiliary details do not turn into fatal runtime failures. Host and container memory readers have been refactored into stateless helpers, and related error reporting has been cleaned up and prefixed consistently.

On the CPU side, bare-metal `/proc/stat` parsing is corrected to use specific enumerated fields and avoid double-counting. The runtime now maintains global cached CPU state and reports CPU utilization as a smoothed, time-aware moving average rather than an instantaneous sample. The new model is better suited for operator-facing reporting and long-running process decisions, and it also supports CPU throttling (cgroup v2).

The CLI reflects these changes directly. `ais show cluster` now shows **SYS CPU(%)** instead of load average by default, moves load averages behind `--verbose`, and adds **THROTTLED(%)** when the displayed proxy or target section contains at least one non-zero cgroup-v2 throttling value.

The last part of the work addresses deployment realism. On Kubernetes, cgroup-v2 files may live under per-pod subtrees rather than fixed global paths, so AIS now resolves `/sys/fs/cgroup` paths at init time instead of hardcoding them. Startup logging also returns a more descriptive container tag, and the implementation includes explicit constrained-container testing and documentation.

### Commits

* [dd03cae2c](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/dd03cae2c): sys: bare-metal CPU usage parsing (fix)
* [1b1397ee3](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/1b1397ee3): sys: cpu and memory (part two; major)
* [3fb3aeb7e](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/3fb3aeb7e): sys: cpu and memory (support cgroup-v2 memory stats)
* [ac6c9461a](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/ac6c9461a): sys: cpu and memory (cgroup v2 in a constrained container)
* [074554a72](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/074554a72): sys: CPU utilization is now a moving average; [API change]
* [30e7f430a](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/30e7f430a): sys: cpu and memory (resolve `/sys/fs/cgroup/` paths at init time)
* [366a8906e](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/366a8906e): cli: show CPU utilization (EMA); load-averages only when verbose

<a name="native-bucket-inventory-nbi"></a>
## Native Bucket Inventory (NBI)

[Native bucket inventory](/docs/nbi.md) was introduced in 4.3. In **4.4**, it becomes the clear and supported path for AIS-managed inventory-backed listing.

The most visible functional addition is support for **non-recursive inventory listing** via `--nr`. That closes an important gap for users who want inventory-backed listing while preserving delimiter-style behavior rather than flattening the namespace unconditionally.

Just as importantly, 4.4 removes the older **S3-specific inventory** implementation and routes S3-compatible inventory-backed requests to NBI instead. This includes removal of deprecated S3-only backend hooks, old R-flow plumbing, and deprecated CLI/API pieces such as `--s3-inventory`. At the S3 compatibility layer, AIS keeps the existing `Ais-Bucket-Inventory` and `Ais-Inv-Name` headers, but now interprets them through NBI with validation.

With 4.4, NBI is no longer experimental. The docs are updated accordingly; 4.4 adds benchmark tooling and documentation around large-bucket listing to support that shift in status.

### Commits

* [ddbca5e78](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/ddbca5e78): native bucket inventory: support non-recursive mode (`--nr`)
* [95b023365](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/95b023365): remove legacy S3 inventory; route S3 compat to NBI; update docs
* [8cab32fcf](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/8cab32fcf): perf: add NBI benchmark python script; update docs
* [b06d42815](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/b06d42815): blog: native bucket inventory blog

<a name="s3-compatibility-and-remote-bucket-discovery"></a>
## S3 Compatibility and Remote Bucket Discovery

4.4 also improves general S3 usability outside NBI.

First, AIS now uses **`HeadBucket` for region discovery**. When the bucket region is initially unknown, the discovered region is propagated back into the session and used to construct a new client with the now-complete connection tuple. This also removes an older special workaround and includes a `ListBuckets()` special case when credentials do not provide a region. The overall effect is simpler and more reliable region handling for S3 buckets.

Second, 4.4 improves the behavior and messaging when users try to add a **inaccessible S3 bucket**, including clearer guidance for cases such as explicitly specifying `extra.aws.cloud_region`.

Third, AIS now returns more standard **S3 error codes**. The S3 layer introduces structured error information via `s3.ErrInfo` and consistently reports codes such as `NoSuchKey`, `NoSuchBucket`, and `NoSuchUpload`, including `NoSuchKey` for GET, HEAD, DELETE, and COPY of non-existent objects.

### Commits

* [829559e73](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/829559e73): s3: use HeadBucket for region discovery
* [db3a5a4a5](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/db3a5a4a5): s3 compat: return standard S3 error codes (NoSuchKey, et al.)

---

<a name="oci-backend"></a>
## OCI Backend

The OCI backend gains two notable capabilities in 4.4.

First, AIS now supports **per-bucket OCI regions** via `extra.oci.region`. Backend operations are routed through region-keyed clients, making it possible to use different OCI regions on a bucket-by-bucket basis rather than relying on a single process-wide assumption.

Second, AIS adds native **instance principal authentication** via `OCI_INSTANCE_PRINCIPAL_AUTH`. The implementation also serializes OCI client creation per region, adds regression tests, and extends CLI autocompletion for `extra.oci.*`. Because this is marked as a **BMD change**, it belongs in the upgrade notes as well.

### Commits

* [ac35234f9](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/ac35234f9): [BMD change] oci: support per-bucket regions and instance principal auth

---

<a name="bucket-metadata-and-bmd-changes"></a>
## Bucket Metadata and BMD Changes

4.4 introduces `extra.custom`, a new **per-bucket user-defined metadata** field in `ExtraProps`.

The new field is an opaque string, up to 128 characters, settable via bucket properties APIs. Validation rejects control characters and enforces a maximum length consistently across providers. CLI help and usage examples are updated accordingly, and bucket-property error messages now include unmarshal details to make bad inputs easier to diagnose. This change is also marked as a **BMD change**.

### Commits

* [fed41c850](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/fed41c850): [BMD change] add `extra.custom`: per-bucket user-defined metadata; cli help

<a name="cli"></a>
## CLI

Most visible CLI work in 4.4 is tied to the runtime and NBI changes already described above.

The cluster view now defaults to **SYS CPU(%)**, moves load averages behind `--verbose`, and conditionally shows throttling when the displayed proxy or target section contains at least one non-zero cgroup-v2 throttling value. The cluster table also hides the **REBALANCE** column when no rebalance is running, reducing noise in the common case. CLI docs and examples have been refreshed to match current output.

The feature-flags documentation is also updated to reflect current code, including the addition of the `deploy` tag and replacement of the removed `System-Reserved` flag with `Force-Container-CPU-Mem`. In addition, OCI property autocompletion and `extra.custom` usage are surfaced through the CLI.

<a name="python-sdk-and-etl"></a>
## Python SDK and ETL

This short cycle includes one focused ETL fix and some documentation work on the Python side.

The ETL change improves direct-put error handling by adding an explicit FastAPI handler for transient ETL direct-put failures, returning **502 Bad Gateway** where appropriate and avoiding pointless retries on `ConnectionRefused`. Tests are updated accordingly.

On the documentation side, AIS now adds separate documents for the **parallel downloader** and **content iterator**, continuing the broader Python SDK documentation work that started in earlier releases.

<a name="tracing"></a>
## Tracing

Tracing gets two small but important correctness fixes in 4.4.

AIS no longer silently ignores failures to load the tracing access token. In addition, self-signed certificate handling is corrected so that `skip verify` no longer disables TLS entirely; instead, TLS remains enabled while certificate verification is relaxed appropriately for that configuration.

### Commits

* [9acdcf349](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/9acdcf349): tracing: do not silently ignore a failure to load access token

## Website

4.4 migrates the AIStore project website from Jekyll to Fern.

The new setup adds Fern configuration (`docs.yml`, `fern.config.json`, NVIDIA theme), a `generate-pages.sh` script that auto-generates `fern/pages/` from the existing `docs/` tree, and Python helpers for documentation navigation, blog navigation, blog index generation, and MDX escaping. New Makefile targets (`fern-generate`, `fern-preview`, `fern-build`) support local development.

A new GitHub Actions workflow handles automatic publishing on pushes to `main`, triggering only when `docs/`, `fern/`, `scripts/fern/`, or `README.md` change.

## Build, CI, and Tools

Assorted dependency updates include `aws-sdk-go-v2` and the indirect `go-jose` dependency (security fixes).

<a name="upgrade-notes"></a>
## Upgrade Notes

### NBI replaces the legacy S3-specific inventory path

The older S3-specific inventory implementation has been removed. Inventory-backed S3 compatibility requests now route through **native bucket inventory (NBI)** instead, while preserving the `Ais-Bucket-Inventory` and `Ais-Inv-Name` headers. Users relying on deprecated S3-only inventory plumbing or `--s3-inventory` should migrate to NBI-based workflows.

### CPU reporting semantics have changed

AIS now reports CPU utilization as a **smoothed moving average** rather than the previous instantaneous/load-oriented presentation. Related API fields are exposed through `apc.MemCPUInfo`, and the CLI reflects this by default. Operators should expect cluster CPU output to look different after upgrade.

### BMD changes

This release includes two distinct **BMD changes**:

* OCI backend support for per-bucket regions and instance principal authentication
* `extra.custom` per-bucket user-defined metadata in bucket properties

### Go toolchain

Contributors and builders should note that 4.4 transitions the project to **Go 1.26**.

### Website

The project website has migrated from Jekyll to Fern. Contributors working on documentation should note the new build targets (`make fern-generate`, `make fern-preview`, `make fern-build`). The `docs/` directory remains the single source of truth.

# AIStore 4.5 Release Notes

Source: https://github.com/nvidia/aistore/blob/main/docs/relnotes/4.5.md

# AIStore 4.5 Release Notes

AIStore **4.5** is a focused release on three major areas: [global rebalance](#global-rebalance) scalability, indexed archive access via the new [shard index](#shard-index), and a [get-batch](#get-batch) flow reordering that substantially reduces memory pressure under load.

The work on global rebalance is one of the headlines. AIS removes the legacy per-object ACK machinery that had become a scalability ceiling for very large rebalances (counting millions of migrated objects), replaces the cleanup behavior that depended on that machinery with a new explicit cleanup mode, and optimizes the lifecycle around data movers, transport endpoints, stage transitions, and peer status queries.

Remote list-objects (R-flow) is another practical driver for this release. Multi-target remote-bucket listing now starts the `(N - 1)` targets _before_ the designated target (DT) begins backend listing and page distribution. The same area also gets flow-control cleanup, corrected page accounting, and a dedicated CLI job view for remote-list xactions.

The shard index is a new experimental subsystem for indexed extraction from TAR shards. It lets GET and [get-batch](#get-batch) read files from TAR shards directly using a persisted index instead of scanning the full archive. The 4.5 implementation includes the index format and binary pack/unpack support, persistence in a system bucket, a bucket-scoped indexing xaction, CLI support, read-path integration, tests, and a micro-benchmark.

Streaming get-batch responses now use explicit write deadlines while sending data to the client. This lets AIS detect terminated, stalled, or unreachable clients promptly and abort the request instead of continuing to assemble and transmit a large batch that no client is still reading. The flow was reordered and optimized, work-item cancellation now propagates across senders, and admission control is stricter under load.

[Authentication and access control](#authn) adds support for externally provisioned RSA signing keys, JWKS refresh on cache miss for rotated key pairs, configurable maximum token age, and a more general signing-key configuration. Intra-cluster request validation is also tightened: spoofed caller headers are rejected on the public network, and internal-network checks require a validated Smap entry.

CLI and observability gain several user-visible improvements: dynamic `ais show cluster cpu` and `ais show cluster memory` views, a new `ais performance intra-data` view, shard-index commands, better rebalance rendering including cleanup mode, and improved help for force-join / split-brain recovery workflows.

This release preserves backward compatibility.
The few additive API fields, configurable behavior changes, and operational migration notes are summarized in [Upgrade Notes](#upgrade-notes).

<a name="global-rebalance"></a>
## Global Rebalance

AIStore 4.5 delivers the largest rebalance update in several release cycles. The main theme is replacing per-object state with stage-level coordination and explicit cleanup semantics.

### Per-object ACKs removed

Rebalance no longer tracks individual object acknowledgments. The previous mechanism - ACK messages back to the sender, sender-side maps of unacknowledged objects, retransmit and wait loops, and an ACK-driven lazy-delete path - has been removed in favor of stage-level coordination.

In the new model, traversal sends objects without keeping per-object state on the sender, and a post-traverse barrier takes the place of the old wait-for-ACK drain. Intra-cluster transport headers carry a compact opaque payload with the rebalance generation, so receivers can recognize and reject objects that arrive late from a previous run. Object and byte totals reported by `ais show rebalance` and `ais show job` now come directly from the transmitted counters rather than from ACK accounting.

The practical effect is lower memory pressure and simpler lifecycle behavior during large rebalances, where per-object ACK state had become the limiting factor.

### Cleanup mode

Removing per-object ACKs also removed the old incidental mechanism that trimmed misplaced source copies after migration. AIStore 4.5 adds an explicit replacement: **rebalance cleanup mode**.

Cleanup mode walks local mountpaths, identifies misplaced object copies using Smap HRW ownership, and removes a misplaced copy only after verifying that the canonical copy exists in the expected location with matching object identity. Identity checks include size and checksum, and use version / ETag when available.

CLI:

```console
$ ais start rebalance --cleanup
$ ais start rebalance --cleanup --force
```

By default, cleanup mode keeps diverged copies. With `--force`, it can also remove copies that differ from the canonical peer version. This is an advanced operator option.

Cleanup mode is intentionally distinct from regular rebalance:

* it has its own preflight checks;
* it refuses to start while rebalance or resilver is active;
* it requires at least two active targets;
* it bypasses `config.Rebalance.Enabled`;
* it uses no data mover, no streams, and no GFN;
* it skips EC-enabled buckets and busy objects.

`ais show job` and `ais show rebalance` render cleanup-mode runs with a dedicated view that reports removed objects and bytes rather than migration TX/RX counters.

### Lifecycle and transport

A series of lifecycle changes makes rebalance more robust through abort, preempt, renew, and finalization paths: fresh data mover construction per run, safer handling of duplicate transport endpoints after abort, narrower mutex scope in the finalization path, a consistent same-targets predicate across preempt and renew, and corrected stage-reached detection.

One change is operator-visible: rebalance `CtlMsg` now carries per-stage timing and final status, and `ais show job --all` continues to surface this information after the run completes.

> `CtlMsg` is the control-message interface supported by AIS xactions (jobs). Each xaction uses it to report job-specific runtime state - counters, stage information, start parameters, and error summaries - so that `ais show job` and related commands can render a current view without requiring separate CLI plumbing for every xaction.

### See also

- [`docs/rebalance.md`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/blob/main/docs/rebalance.md) - user-facing guide: concepts, configuration, and CLI workflows including cleanup mode.
- [`reb/README.md`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/blob/main/reb/README.md) - internal design notes: execution flow, stages, and lifecycle.

<a name="shard-index"></a>
## Shard Index

> Experimental in 4.5. The on-disk format, xaction semantics, and CLI surface may change in subsequent releases.

The shard index is a new subsystem for indexed archive extraction, primarily intended for ML and data-lake workloads that repeatedly fetch named samples from large TAR shards. When a client requests a file inside a TAR shard via `archpath`, AIS can now resolve the lookup through a persisted index rather than scanning the archive. The fast path is integrated into both GET and get-batch.

A shard index is a compact binary structure built in a single pass over a source TAR. It supports USTAR, GNU, and PAX variants, encodes entries with `Pack`/`Unpack`, and embeds the source object's checksum and size so the index can detect re-uploads and treat itself as stale when the underlying shard has changed. Indexes are persisted as objects in a new system bucket (`ais://.sys-shardidx`); shards that have an index carry a dedicated flag in their on-disk metadata.

Indexing is performed by a bucket-scoped xaction (job). It walks the bucket, skips non-TAR objects, rebuilds stale or corrupted indexes, and treats per-object failures as non-fatal - a single bad shard does not abort the run.

Index presence, lookup, validation, and fallback are handled entirely by AIS; clients continue to use the same requests to read archived content.

> On the read path, index use is gated by a dedicated bit in each shard's on-disk metadata. That bit is set and cleared atomically together with the index object in the system bucket.
> When the bit is set, AIS loads the index and seeks directly to the requested entry; otherwise the read falls back to the existing sequential archive traversal, with no functional difference visible to the client.

### CLI

```console
$ ais shard-index ais://my-shards
$ ais show shard-index ais://my-shards/object.tar
```

The release also includes a micro-benchmark for indexed extraction and an integration test that runs both indexed and non-indexed variants of `TestGetFromArch` and `TestMoss` and asserts result equivalence.

* [05df64267](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/05df64267): cmn/archive: add TAR shard index
* [ed1ec6977](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/ed1ec6977): cmn/archive: `Pack`/`Unpack` for TAR shard index via compact binary
* [08db651bb](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/08db651bb): shard index: embed source cksum and size; detect stale index on load

<a name="get-batch"></a>
## Get-Batch

The 4.5 cycle continues the work on get-batch - proxy memory pressure under load, sender behavior under failure, admission control, and streaming response reliability.

### Redirect before sender fan-out

The flow is reordered so that the client redirect to the designated target happens before sender fan-out, with fan-out then running asynchronously. Previously the proxy held assembly-related state while waiting for sender startup; the new ordering moves that ownership to the designated target and reduces proxy-side memory pressure substantially.

### Work-item cancellation

A new abort opcode over the target-to-target control path lets the designated target cancel an already-failed work item across all senders. This bounds wasted sender work under error and overload conditions. The cancellation path includes sender-side negative caching of aborted work IDs with periodic cleanup.

### Admission control

Get-Batch admission control now accounts for pending work items and system load more directly. Critical memory or disk pressure returns HTTP 429. High memory pressure combined with a high pending-work level can throttle or reject depending on severity. The intent is to keep throughput steady in normal conditions while making overload behavior predictable.

### Streaming responses

Get-batch streaming responses can run for a long time as the designated target (DT) assembles and writes the output. If a client terminates or simply stops reading mid-stream, AIS now detects this promptly and stops the assembly, rather than continuing to do reassembly work into a socket nobody is reading from. The implementation sets explicit write deadlines on the response stream so that a hung write fails fast and surfaces the abandoned client to the xaction.

### Phase-3 startup acknowledgment

Senders acknowledge phase-3 startup to the designated target over the T2T control path. The designated target tracks expected senders per work item and fails the request if startup acknowledgments don't arrive within the startup window - turning a class of silent hangs into prompt, observable failures. Object transfer still uses SDM; only the startup notification moves to the control path.

### Observability

Get-Batch xaction IDs are now prefixed `gbt-` for easier identification in CLI output and logs. CtlMsg output separates job-level and node-level counters, and per-work-item CtlMsg is surfaced on assembly errors and in super-verbose mode.

* [34a48d0ec](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/34a48d0ec): get-batch: admission control (bump num-pending-high-wm)

<a name="intra-cluster-control-plane"></a>
## Intra-Cluster Control Plane

AIS 4.5 continues separating data-plane traffic from xaction control traffic and tightens validation of requests that claim to be intra-cluster.

### Remote List-Objects (R-flow)

Multi-target remote-bucket list-objects - the "R-flow" mechanism, one of several distinct list-objects paths in AIS - gets a startup-ordering fix and an accounting cleanup.

> In a multi-target R-flow run, one target is designated to perform the backend listing and distribute pages to the others. In 4.5, DT waits a brief grace period before issuing the backend call and beginning page distribution. This is a temporary workaround until the flow gets a proper prepare phase.

Separately, the list-objects flow-control code is cleaned up - local context is threaded through where it was previously passed implicitly - and page-receive accounting is made consistent between DM and the list-objects xaction so that received pages are no longer double-counted.

Further, list-objects jobs now get dedicated `ais show job` rendering, including a remote-pagination view with TX/RX page counters.

### Target-to-target xaction control path

A generic target-to-target xaction control path is added under:

```text
POST /v1/xactions/t2tctrl/{kind}/{xid}/{wid}/{opcode}
```

It runs over `cmn.NetIntraControl` and is used by get-batch for sender-started notifications and abort propagation, keeping get-batch control messages off the SDM data path. Future xactions that need out-of-band control signaling can use the same route.

### Intra-cluster request validation

Requests that claim intra-cluster identity are now validated more strictly. Caller headers received on the public network are rejected; self-joining nodes may still use the public network but those headers are stripped from their requests. Internal-network checks require a validated current-Smap entry, so a node that isn't in the current cluster map can't claim intra-cluster status.

Underlying these checks, `/reverse`, `/cluster`, and `/daemon` each gain separate public and intra-control entry points, with public entry points performing access checks before dispatching. The split makes it harder for an external client to spoof intra-cluster identity or bypass public access controls.

### Error propagation

`ErrHTTP` handling is reinforced across proxy and target boundaries. Forwarded HTTP errors now preserve their original status codes - previously, certain forwarded errors had their status overwritten, which broke clients (including the Python SDK) that retry on specific codes such as 429 from admission control.

<a name="authn"></a>
## AuthN

Authentication gets several changes around RSA signing keys, JWKS, and token validation.

RSA signing configuration is restructured under `auth.rsa.{bits,mode}`. The new `mode: "external"` setting indicates that the RSA signing key is managed outside the AuthN process, which is useful for multi-replica deployments, secret managers, and HSM-backed key management.

In external mode:

* a missing key file at startup is fatal;
* AuthN does not auto-generate the key;
* `POST /v1/auth/keys/rotate` returns 400;
* JWKS is built from the key file during initialization;
* live reload still requires restart.

JWKS lookup now supports rotated key pairs better: on key-cache miss, AuthN refreshes from the issuer before failing validation. A new `max_token_age` config option decouples JWKS cache age from token expiration.

The older environment-controlled signing-mode mechanism is removed in favor of the explicit config model.

### Commits

* [0caf82d3b](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/0caf82d3b): authn: RSA config restructured under auth.rsa; externally provisioned key support (#294)

* [88917b7c9](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/88917b7c9): auth: support rotated key pairs with JWKS refresh on cache miss
* [3a2c527cc](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/3a2c527cc): authn: add max_token_age config option and decouple jwks max-age from token expiry

<a name="stats-and-observability"></a>
## Stats and Observability

### GET-not-found stats: now off by default

GET(object) 404s are no longer counted in error stats by default. This avoids inflating Prometheus error counters for workloads where object-not-found is expected or common (probe-then-PUT patterns, content-addressed lookups, etc.).

Operators that prefer the previous behavior can enable the `Count-Object-NotFound-Stats` [feature flag](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/blob/main/docs/feature_flags.md) at cluster or bucket scope.

> See [Upgrade Notes](#upgrade-notes) for the CLI invocation.

### Cgroup v2 memory pressure

The cgroup v2 actual-free memory estimate is refined to use total file-backed cache minus dirty/writeback pages. This improves memory-pressure signaling in containerized deployments - particularly under heavy write load, where the previous estimate could overcount reclaimable memory.

### Cluster CPU and memory views

`apc.MemCPUInfo` gains structured memory and process-stat fields. The existing flat fields remain, and the new fields are optional. The CLI uses the richer structure to render the new `ais show cluster cpu` and `ais show cluster memory` views - see [CLI](#cli) for examples.

### Intra-data performance view

A new `ais performance intra-data` view reports intra-cluster data movement separately from generic stream counters: per-target RX/TX object counts, bytes, throughput, and average object size, with cluster-wide totals and an idle indicator.

To support the view, transport and DM counters now count data PDUs only - control-message PDUs no longer contribute. This is a small behavior change for anyone reading existing transport counters: numbers shown in `ais show job` and the generic stream views may be slightly lower than they were under 4.4 for the same workload, with the difference accounted for as control traffic.

### Msgpack-encoded stats

`stats.NodeStatus` and related control-plane structures can now be encoded as msgpack as an alternative to JSON. Clients opt in via `Accept: application/msgpack`; clients that don't continue to receive JSON. The motivation is lower allocation and faster decoding on hot stats-collection paths.

* [f52af0a2b](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/f52af0a2b): [API change]: add structured memory and process stats; cli: 'ais show cluster'
* [80a8c459e](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/80a8c459e): GET(object) not found is now not counted by default; new feature flag
* [ac37f2e33](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/ac37f2e33): sys: refine cgroup v2 'actual-free' estimate for memory pressure

<a name="blob-downloader-and-prefetch"></a>
## Blob Downloader and Prefetch

### Per-chunk read timeout and abort propagation

The blob downloader gains a per-chunk backend read timeout: `BlobMsg.ChunkReadTimeout` is a new optional field (zero selects the default); the GET path can also pass it via `apc.HdrBlobReadTimeout`.

Per-range reads now derive their context from the xaction context, so aborting the xaction cancels in-flight backend readers and body copies. Error paths close range readers consistently.

### Admission and adaptive parallelism

Blob-download jobs now go through the same load-aware admission and worker-tuning that other heavy-duty xactions (list-range, TCB) use. At job start, AIS checks memory, CPU, and goroutine load. Under critical memory pressure the job is refused with HTTP 429; under high pressure, start may be briefly delayed and the worker count is reduced.

Worker count itself is the minimum of three caps: the load-tuned count (which folds in the user request, mountpath count, media type, and live system load), an object-size cap of roughly one worker per 256 MiB of data, and a hard ceiling. So a small object on a fast disk gets a single worker even if the user asks for more; a multi-GiB object on NVMe scales up; nothing exceeds the hard cap. The same heuristic now backs blob-download, list-range jobs, and TCB.

### Prefetch integration

Prefetch decides per-object whether to use the blob-downloader: any object at or above `BlobThreshold` (when configured) is fetched as a BLOB, otherwise as a normal cold GET.

Starting prefetch on a large remote bucket can therefore spawn a series of blob-download jobs autonomously - which is why the admission and worker-tuning improvements above matter most in this context. Each blob-download job runs through the same checks, so a prefetch fan-out adapts to live memory, CPU, and disk pressure rather than launching workers blindly.

Prefetch can now pass blob-downloader worker and chunk-size settings through to the underlying jobs:

```console
$ ais prefetch ... --blob-chunk-size <size> --blob-num-workers <n>
```

### Commits

* [28b6ee302](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/28b6ee302): [API change] blob-downloader: per-chunk read timeout and context-driven abort
* [5788880fe](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/5788880fe): blob-downloader: refactor and cleanup; revise throttling logic
* [19c0bfa6b](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/19c0bfa6b): xs/blob_download: cap blob-download workers with prefetch

<a name="core-config-and-xactions"></a>
## Core, Config, and xactions

### Chunk-size validation

Chunk-size constants are exported, and bucket-config validation now backfills and checks `chunks.chunk_size` even when automatic chunking is disabled. This prevents legacy bucket properties from persisting `ChunkSize == 0` and later causing divide-by-zero paths on oversized PUT or cold GET.

### Workfile basename overflow

Workfile creation now handles borderline-length object names safely. If decorated temporary workfile names would exceed filesystem basename limits, AIS shortens the temporary basename while preserving the final object path.

### Force-join target initialization

Joining targets now create bucket directories during force-join commit before installing the destination BMD. This prevents missing local bucket directories after cross-cluster force-join workflows.

### Space cleanup

Space cleanup now distinguishes local mountpath placement from cluster-wide HRW ownership. A locally well-placed object can still be cluster-misplaced after rebalance or target rejoin; cleanup now detects that case and removes the local stale copy only after the cluster-HRW peer confirms identical content.

This complements, but does not replace, rebalance cleanup mode. `ais space-cleanup` remains a local cleanup tool; `ais start rebalance --cleanup` is the explicit cluster-wide cleanup workflow for misplaced object copies.

Space cleanup also skips chunk manifests as a temporary safeguard.

### Cloud/backend fixes

AWS multipart upload now handles S3 client creation failure. OCI region header spelling is canonicalized.

<a name="python-sdk-etl-and-aisloader"></a>
## Python SDK, ETL, and aisloader

### Python SDK v1.24.0

The Python SDK release includes several reliability and compatibility fixes:

* `RetryConfig` and `RetryManager` are picklable, unblocking PyTorch `DataLoader` workers under spawn/forkserver-style multiprocessing;
* object reads retry after clean short EOF by resuming from the current byte offset;
* retry logging emits the final exhausted-retry stack once, while preserving concise per-attempt warnings;
* the legacy `aistore/client.py` compatibility re-export is removed;
* missing `__init__.py` files are added to SDK subpackages so generated API docs include the expected modules.

### ETL streaming

ETL streaming paths are tightened across FastAPI, Flask, and HTTPMultiThreadedServer implementations.

Highlights:

* no-FQN FastAPI hpull GET streams through the shared session without buffering the full upstream object;
* no-FQN FastAPI hpush PUT bridges async request streams into sync readers for constant-memory `transform_stream` consumption;
* HTTPMultiThreadedServer hpush PUT uses a bounded reader around `rfile` and drains unread bytes on close to preserve keep-alive correctness;
* one-shot no-FQN PUT bodies skip local retry and rely on AIS-level retry when the server returns the direct-put transient signal;
* transient direct-put bailouts return `503` with `Ais-Etl-Retry-Reason: direct-put-transient`; exhausted-retry cases continue to use `502`.

### Python tests

Test infrastructure is cleaned up to reduce flakes:

* FastAPI ETL tests eager-import `pydantic.v1` on Python 3.9 to avoid an importlib race;
* environment mutations are scoped to avoid leakage between xdist workers;
* sync and async FastAPI ETL tests are split according to how they exercise the server.

### aisloader

`aisloader` adds `-arch.list` to enable read-only archpath-selective get-batch listing with `-pctput=0`. `-arch.pct > 0` continues to imply archive listing.

<a name="upgrade-notes"></a>
## Upgrade Notes

### AuthN config migration

The top-level `rsa_key_bits` and `externally_provisioned` settings are replaced by the `auth.rsa.{bits,mode}` config block.

Use:

```json
{
  "auth": {
    "rsa": {
      "bits": 2048,
      "mode": "external"
    }
  }
}
```

for externally provisioned RSA keys.

In external mode, a missing key file at startup is fatal and key rotation through `POST /v1/auth/keys/rotate` returns 400. Environment-controlled signing mode is removed in favor of explicit config.

### Additive APIs

The following API changes are additive and backward-compatible for existing JSON clients:

* `BlobMsg.ChunkReadTimeout` - optional per-chunk backend read timeout for blob downloader; zero selects the default;
* `apc.HdrBlobReadTimeout` - optional GET-path header for blob read timeout;
* `apc.MemCPUInfo` gains optional structured memory and process stats;
* `Accept: application/msgpack` requests msgpack for selected stats/control-plane structures; clients that do not request it continue to receive JSON.

### GET-not-found stats

GET(object) 404s are no longer counted in error stats by default. This avoids inflating Prometheus error counters for workloads where object-not-found responses are expected.

To preserve the previous behavior, enable the `Count-Object-NotFound-Stats` feature flag at cluster or bucket scope.

Example:

```console
$ ais config cluster set features=Count-Object-NotFound-Stats
```

### Stream bundle API cleanup

Stream bundles no longer listen for Smap changes and no longer support listener-driven resync APIs such as `ManualResync` or `ListenSmapChanged`. Internal callers should pass the intended Smap at construction time and use `DM.Smap()` when they need to inspect the pinned Smap.

### Shard index is experimental

Shard index is available in 4.5 but remains experimental. The index format, xaction behavior, and CLI surface may change in a later release.

### Rebalance cleanup mode

`ais start rebalance --cleanup` is the new explicit cluster-wide path for safely removing misplaced object copies. It is separate from regular rebalance and from local space cleanup.

Use `--force` only when intentionally removing diverged misplaced copies after verifying that this is the desired operator action.

# AIStore 4.6 Release Notes

Source: https://github.com/nvidia/aistore/blob/main/docs/relnotes/4.6.md

# AIStore 4.6 Release Notes

AIStore **4.6** is a short-cycle reliability and scalability release following 4.5.

The drivers are practical: stabilize get-batch under heavy ML-style stress, replace the list-objects [startup grace period](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/releases/tag/v1.4.5#intra-cluster-control-plane) with an explicit two-phase commit (2PC) protocol, avoid cgroup-v2 broadcast throttling in large clusters, harden primary-restart bootstrap, guard against prefetch misconfiguration, and make prefetch/blob-downloader behavior easier to observe and control.

Get-Batch is the largest area of work. Under heavy ML-style load - many concurrent batch requests, large objects, slow or disconnecting clients - the prior implementation could leak work items, take too long to abort, or mishandle late arrivals after cleanup. The 4.6 changes restructure the work-item lifecycle around explicit ownership, receive-side pinning, progress-based cleanup timers, bounded abort latency, and stricter late-arrival rejection.

Remote list-objects, also referred to as `R-flow`, gets a structural fix. The temporary startup-grace workaround from 4.5 is replaced with an explicit begin/commit/abort sequence: targets that are about to receive pages prepare first, the randomly selected *designated target* starts paging only after the receive side is ready, and abort has a dedicated cleanup path.

Broadcast parallelism in containerized deployments is also improved. In deployments using cgroup-v2 CPU quotas, a proxy with a small visible CPU count could collapse one-to-many broadcasts to single-digit parallelism even when targeting dozens of targets. A dedicated cluster broadcast wait group now covers the mostly I/O-bound intra-cluster fanout paths: keepalive, rebalance, generic broadcasts, and xaction target-to-target control.

The intra-cluster control plane is faster on the hot path. Keepalives and broadcasts - invoked behind essentially every cluster operation - no longer register a timer, allocate a context, and defer a cancel on every call. A separate fix covers a former primary restarting without a local cluster map: rather than assuming the primary role from local configuration alone, the proxy probes alternative URLs and validates returned node-state-info first.

Prefetch and blob-downloader observability is another release driver. A single prefetch job can spawn many blob-download child jobs. The 4.6 release adds clearer parent/child reporting, per-xaction stats, bucket-keyed Prometheus metrics, and rejection counters so operators can understand progress and throttling behavior without correlating logs manually. Get-Batch and list-objects extend their control-message output in the same direction. The cross-cutting picture is summarized in [Observability](#observability).

No data-format migration is required. Operational and API behavior changes are summarized in [Upgrade Notes](#upgrade-notes).

<a name="get-batch"></a>

## Get-Batch

### Work-item lifecycle

Get-Batch is highly concurrent by design: a single [x-moss xaction](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/blob/main/docs/get_batch.md) multiplexes many batch requests, each driven by a remote client. A slow or disconnected client can leave its work item parked on the target side - receivers still pinned, SGLs still held - while making no forward progress. We call these *abandoned* work items; detecting them reliably without falsely killing legitimately slow batches is one of the problems 4.6 addresses.

Work-item ownership is now an explicit three-state model rather than a single demand flag. Assembly claims a work item before consuming it; abandoned-work GC may clean only unowned work; and receive paths use pin/unpin discipline, so data and control receives cannot accidentally keep touching a work item that is already cleaning up or abandoned.

Abandoned work items are marked before cleanup, and new receives are rejected once cleanup begins. Cleanup waits for a stable receive/assembly quiet window, using last-receive and last-assembly progress timestamps rather than only the original start time. This matters for large batches that can legitimately run for a long time while still making forward progress.

The work-item memory pool (sync.Pool) is removed in favor of explicit receive-side pin/unpin. The housekeeper gets a dedicated x-moss maintenance callback, so abandoned-work cleanup no longer depends on the generic [DemandBase](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/blob/main/xact/demand.go) idle/fini path, and each cleanup pass is capped so the housekeeper remains responsive.

The shared data-mover (SDM) receive-side lock ordering is tightened as well: the receiver-demux mutex is no longer held across `Close()`, and Rx drop now distinguishes SDM close from xaction abort.

### Abort and late-arrival handling

Abort latency is now bounded. An unbounded `wait-group.Wait()` is replaced with a bounded poll, and `drainRx` is extracted with a `brief` mode for fast cleanup paths. Stuck receive-side work items are forced through cleanup via the abandoned path. Late assembly is rejected after x-moss is aborted or done; late `Assemble` calls after abort cleanup are tolerated; and internal stopped sentinels are treated as quiet assembly termination.

Stop/Abort terminal semantics are tightened. `DemandBase.Stop` is now idempotent and protected by its own atomic, and the common `SetStopping` returns its CAS result so get-batch can use it to eliminate a race against its own concurrent Abort. `DemandBase.Stop` is now called before waiting and quiescing.

*Get-from-neighbor (GFN)* is the internal target-to-target object-fetch path, used both during global rebalance, when objects migrate between targets, and by get-batch when a target needs an object it does not have locally. GFN error handling is corrected as well. When get-batch engages GFN, not-found remains a soft error while other GFN failures are treated as hard errors. Membership changes are detected and enforced during hole-timeout and failed-GFN paths, so a target-set change no longer looks like an ordinary object-level miss.

### Observability and docs

Control messages now include target IDs and use clearer formatting. Documentation is updated to clarify supported scope and known limitations.

<a name="list-objects"></a>

## Remote List-Objects (R-flow)

Multi-target remote-bucket list-objects - the `R-flow` mechanism, one of several distinct list-objects paths in AIS - gains the explicit prepare phase anticipated in the 4.5 release notes.

> In a multi-target R-flow run, one target is designated to perform the backend listing and distribute pages to the others. In 4.5, the designated target waited a brief grace period before issuing the backend call and beginning page distribution - a temporary workaround until the flow gained an explicit prepare phase.

The workaround is replaced with an explicit two-phase protocol. The begin phase broadcasts startup, renews the x-lso, opens streams, and registers receive paths. The commit phase performs strict x-lso lookup and starts paging. The abort phase performs best-effort lookup and aborts the xaction if present. The previously reserved feature flag used by the workaround is removed as part of the same cleanup.

The same area gains better runtime observability, extending the dedicated `ais show job` rendering introduced in 4.5. List-objects now reports lightweight per-request statistics: successful pages, returned entries, errors, and average/max page latency. Control messages include the target name and static request details on one selected target, and the implementation retains the startup Smap for stable R-flow execution.

Prometheus-label handling in the page path is also micro-optimized: variable labels are allocated once per xaction rather than per page.

### Commits

* [65b4888df](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/65b4888df): list-objects R-flow is now 2PC
* [9137eb0ba](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/9137eb0ba): list-objects: extend x-lso observability; stabilize cluster map use
* [0d4b15165](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/0d4b15165): list-objects: move Prometheus variable labels (micro-optimize)

<a name="large-cluster-broadcast-scalability"></a>

## Large-Cluster Broadcast Scalability

Intra-cluster broadcast scalability is improved for containerized deployments that use cgroup-v2 CPU quotas.

Previously, broadcast parallelism was tied to the visible CPU count. In deployments where an AIS proxy was assigned a small CPU quota - for example, 8 cores in a cluster of dozens of targets - one-to-many fanout could collapse to single-digit parallelism. This affected mostly I/O-bound control-plane paths: generic broadcasts, keepalive, rebalance, xaction target-to-target control, and EC metadata requests.

A dedicated cluster broadcast wait group now provides a minimum floor of `128`, while the existing limited wait group is preserved for CPU- or disk-bound local work.

The intent is simple: local CPU-bound parallelism should continue to respect CPU availability, but cluster fanout should not be collapsed merely because the proxy is running under a cgroup-v2 CPU quota.

### Commits

* [1f686a475](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/1f686a475): decouple intra-cluster broadcast from CPU cgroup quotas

<a name="intra-cluster-control-plane"></a>

## Intra-Cluster Control Plane

The intra-cluster control plane is micro-optimized, and the public-vs-intra header-stamping work from the previous release is carried further.

### Static control-plane clients

Per-call timeout setup is replaced with statically configured HTTP clients for the two main control-plane timeout classes: keepalive probes and the broadcast timeout used behind essentially every control-plane API. The hot path no longer pays per-call setup cost on every keepalive and broadcast.

The tradeoff is that two configuration knobs - `timeout.cplane_operation` and `timeout.max_keepalive` - now require a node restart to re-apply. CLI updates to these knobs report that restart is required. See [Upgrade Notes](#upgrade-notes).

### Intra-cluster header stamping

The header-stamping rule is inverted from "stamp unless we know it's public" to "stamp only when we know it's intra-control." The new rule is easier to reason about and naturally complements the public/intra validation work from the previous release.

Keepalive also filters redundant heard-from updates in `htrun.call`, avoiding unnecessary writes in paths where the information is already known to be stale or irrelevant. The related `TransportArgs.Timeout` field is renamed to `ClientTimeout` for clarity.

### Commits

* [486f8ab3b](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/486f8ab3b): add two static HTTP clients for intra-cluster control-plane
* [5fb450a59](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/5fb450a59): simplify/refactor intra-cluster header-stamping logic (part three)
* [a0e71d528](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/a0e71d528): keep-alive: filter redundant heard-from updates; chores: rename => ClientTimeout

---

<a name="primary-restart-bootstrap"></a>

## Primary Restart (bootstrap)

Proxy startup is hardened for the case where a former primary restarts without a local cluster map.

The failure mode is subtle but operationally disruptive. A restarted former primary may have no current local cluster metadata, while its local configuration still says that `config.primary_url` points to itself. Before 4.6, that node could interpret the configuration as authority to resume the primary role even after the rest of the cluster had already elected or confirmed a replacement primary.

In the best case, no targets join the stale self-primary; it fails to form a cluster, shuts down, and is immediately restarted again by Kubernetes. In worse cases, the behavior can confuse bootstrap and recovery workflows.

AIS now treats local primary configuration as something to confirm, not as sufficient proof of authority. Before assuming the primary role, the proxy probes alternative URLs and validates returned node-state-info. If it discovers a valid current primary, it clears the stale local primary assumption and joins normally as a secondary.

To support this, the public `/health` endpoint used by external watchdogs can now satisfy bootstrap discovery. A new `QparamPrimaryCii` combines "return node-state-info" with "must be primary," allowing direct confirmation of the alleged primary. The proxy health handler is refactored to parse and validate the three independent query parameters.

See also:

* [Joining a Cluster: Discovery URL](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/blob/main/docs/lifecycle_node.md)

### Commits

* [694b34b85](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/694b34b85): when (former) primary restarts without cluster map
* [5c7e04892](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/5c7e04892): gateway's /health: introduce QparamPrimaryCii (part two)

<a name="prefetch-and-blob-downloader"></a>

## Prefetch and Blob Downloader

Observability for prefetch workloads that use blob-downloader internally is significantly improved.

The field motivation is that one prefetch job can spawn many blob-download child jobs. Without explicit parent/child reporting and per-path counters, it can be difficult to tell whether the system is making progress, throttling blob-download admission, or spending most of its time in cold-GET versus blob-download work.

A misconfigured `blob-threshold` set too small could previously cause a single prefetch job to spawn hundreds of blob-downloaders. AIS now clamps undersized thresholds to `minBlobDlPrefetch` with a warning, keeping the fanout bounded.

Prefetch now reports per-xaction statistics separating cold-GET and blob-downloader paths. Control messages show configured parameters, completed cold/blob work, pending work, and blob-downloader admission rejects. Prometheus metrics are added for object counts, bytes, cumulative latency, blob-downloader rejects, and object-level prefetch errors.

Blob-downloader control messages also identify which caller spawned the download. Possible origins are:

* `GET` - user issued a regular [object GET](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/blob/main/api/object.go) with a flag indicating blob-downloader should be used
* `api-blobdl` - user called the dedicated blob-downloader API directly
* `x-start` - started via the generic xaction-start API
* `parent:prefetch[...]` - spawned by a parent prefetch xaction

For example:

```text
s3://abc/this-current-blob-name parent:prefetch[MSXf3OJpU] chunk-size:4MiB, workers:8
```

The blob-downloader also preserves the full object name at startup for later control-message rendering, avoiding lifetime assumptions about caller-provided LOMs.

### Commits

* [2e3496d4c](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/2e3496d4c): prefetch observability: add internal stats, rewrite CtlMsg
* [57bbe5309](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/57bbe5309): prefetch observability: Prometheus metrics (new); extend control message
* [4739863ea](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/4739863ea): blob-downloader: show parent/origin in control message
* [d4a035b13](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/d4a035b13): blob-downloader: preserve full object name for control message

<a name="space-cleanup"></a>

## Space Cleanup

Space cleanup - [the storage cleanup job](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/blob/main/space/README.md) - is extended to remove stale internal storage entries during the regular cleanup walk, and gets a correctness fix for chunked objects.

System buckets are now routed through dedicated cleanup, and stale shard-index and native bucket inventory entries are removed using source-object liveness checks. System-bucket removals are tracked separately and covered by tests.

Cleanup handling for chunk manifests is also fixed. The cleanup walker now consults the `lmeta` xattr and the `lmflChunk` flag to decide whether to keep or remove chunk metadata. This fixes a silent corruption risk for chunked objects whose names contain dots - `.tar`, `.json`, and similar - which could previously be misidentified as invalid chunk manifests and deleted.

Mountpath walking is refactored so callbacks own LOM loading and lifecycle decisions. The jogger no longer pre-loads or filters copies implicitly; callers (`tcb`, `makencopies`, `nsumm`, `bencodex`, `lom_warmup`, `rechunk`, `shard_idx`) load and handle not-exist cases according to their own semantics.

### Commits

* [27e454b9d](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/27e454b9d): space/cleanup: cleanup orphan system-bucket entries
* [c2b938e49](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/c2b938e49): space cleanup: disambiguate chunk manifests via `lmeta` xattr
* [62edca86a](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/62edca86a): fs/mpather: drop pre-load; callbacks own LOM lifecycle

---

<a name="shard-index-cleanup"></a>

## Shard-Index Cleanup

Shard-index cleanup is added for the case when a shard object is deleted.

When an object with the shard-index flag is removed, the associated index object is now removed from the internal `ais://.sys-shardidx` bucket as well. `LOM.RemoveObj` is refactored to clean secondary storage in one path, including chunks, copies, and shard-index entries.

Shard-index lookup remains transparent to clients. If an index is absent, the system can still fall back to sequential archive traversal. The important consistency rule is that when object metadata says a shard index exists, the corresponding index object must exist as well.

### Commits

* [c2c6883ed](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/c2c6883ed): shard index: remove index when shard object is deleted

<a name="xaction-go-api"></a>

## Xaction Go API

The xaction [descriptor](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/blob/main/xact/api_table.go) gains an explicit Information Center (IC) reporting mode, and the Go xaction wait/status APIs become descriptor-aware.

The descriptor table now distinguishes xactions that report terminal status through IC, xactions that report progress through IC, and xactions that do not report through IC. Go API helpers validate that distinction at the client boundary. IC status/wait helpers fail fast for non-IC xaction kinds, returning the new `cmn.ErrXactNonIC`, instead of silently treating IC as a generic wait mechanism.

> A new [helper](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/blob/main/xact/api_name.go#L50-L78) unifies kind/UUID format validation across xaction API.

A new generic [api.WaitForXaction](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/blob/main/api/xaction.go) dispatches according to descriptor metadata, preserves the full `ArgsMsg` selector, and can wait for idle for xaction kinds that define idling semantics. Tests and tools that used IC wait as a generic wait helper are updated to use descriptor-aware or snaps-based waits for `PutCopies`, `ECPut`, and `Resilver`.

The xaction package [README.md](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/blob/main/xact/README.md) is revised and extended to cover the descriptor table, ICMode, snaps-based status, IC status, waiting semantics, idling, and rebalance/resilver coexistence.

Python SDK alignment with the descriptor-aware semantics is planned for a follow-up.

### Commits

* [354a67129](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/354a67129): extend xaction descriptor - add explicit IC mode (term | progress | none)
* [2d7ef239c](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/2d7ef239c): api/xaction: ICMode-aware status/wait, convenience API, docs (part two)
* [0a5873b9a](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aistore/commit/0a5873b9a): api/xaction: make generic wait descriptor-aware (part three)
